title: Supported conversation for adults with aphasia
text: Training conversation partners to acknowledge competence and reveal it — using writing, drawing, gesture and yes/no questions — measurably improves how well people with aphasia take part in conversation. The person's competence is masked by aphasia, not lost.
source: Kagan A, et al. Training volunteers as conversation partners using Supported Conversation for Adults with Aphasia. J Speech Lang Hear Res 44(3):624–638

title: Communication partner training works
text: A systematic review found communication partner training improves conversation for people with chronic aphasia and changes partner behaviour. Families and carers are effective partners when trained in a few concrete techniques.
source: Simmons-Mackie N, et al. Communication partner training in aphasia: a systematic review. Arch Phys Med Rehabil 91(12):1814–1837

title: Aphasia is a language problem
text: Aphasia affects the use of language — speaking, understanding, reading or writing — after damage to language areas of the brain, usually from stroke. It does not reduce intelligence or memory of who the person is. Speak to the person as the capable adult they remain.
source: National Aphasia Association / ASHA Practice Portal: Aphasia

title: Clear speech, not loud speech
text: For a person with hearing loss, speaking clearly at a natural pace and letting them see your face helps far more than shouting, which distorts the sounds of speech and the shape of the mouth. Reducing background noise and rephrasing missed words are the most useful habits for family members.
source: British Society of Audiology / ASHA: Hearing loss — communication strategies

title: Hearing aids help but do not restore normal hearing
text: Hearing aids make speech more audible but do not return hearing to normal, especially in noise. Good communication habits from the people around the listener, and consistent daily use of well-fitted, charged aids, together give the best everyday result.
source: World Health Organization. World report on hearing
